_meta.scope: Cultural personality dimensions supplementing HEXACO for Japanese norms
_meta.scale_note: RSES means converted to 5-point per-item by Oshio meta-analysis; original RSES is 10 items, 4-point (range 10-40)

collectivism.summary: Common view (Japanese=collectivistic) NOT supported empirically. Hofstede placed Japan mid-range. Takano & Osaka series strongly refute the stereotype. Takada series shows Japanese DO score higher on 相互協調性 than 相互独立性 on self-report, but cross-cultural behavioral comparisons fail to find Japanese > American collectivism.

papers.citation: Takano, Y., & Osaka, E. (1999). An unsupported common view: Comparing Japan and the U.S. on individualism/collectivism. Asian Journal of Social Psychology, 2(3), 311-341.

Takano, Y., & Sogon, S. (2008). Are Japanese more collectivistic than Americans? Examining conformity in in-groups and the reference-group effect. Journal of Cross-Cultural Psychology, 39(3), 237-250.

key_numbers.conclusion: Japanese conform NO MORE than Americans even within their own university club in-groups

papers.citation: Takano, Y., & Osaka, E. (2018). Comparing Japan and the United States on individualism/collectivism: A follow-up review. Asian Journal of Social Psychology, 21(4), 301-316.
高田利武 (1999). 日本文化における相互独立性・相互協調性の発達過程―比較文化的・横断的資料による実証的検討. 教育心理学研究, 47(4), 480-489.

key_numbers.scale: Takada 1996 相互独立的-相互協調的自己観尺度 (each 10 items, 7-point Likert)
key_numbers.key_finding_text: Japanese students: 相互協調性 > 相互独立性 (t(596)=8.61, p<.001). Australian and Canadian students: 相互独立性 > 相互協調性 (t(309)=5.16, t(160)=4.63). Asian-Canadian: no significant difference. Means displayed in Table 6 as image — exact numbers not extractable.

papers.citation: Matsumoto, D. (1999). Culture and self: An empirical assessment of Markus and Kitayama's theory of independent and interdependent self-construals. Asian Journal of Social Psychology, 2(3), 289-310.

key_numbers.main_claim: No study in Markus & Kitayama's cited corpus directly tests their theoretical chain (Culture→Self-construal→Cognition). Studies they cite merely show country-level differences, which can only be interpreted as supporting the theory IF you accept two unverified assumptions about country-self-construal linkage.
key_numbers.supporting_evidence_note: Kleinknecht et al. 1997 finding cited: Americans actually had significantly HIGHER interdependent self-construal scores than Japanese (opposite of theory).

papers.citation: Hofstede Insights / The Culture Factor — country comparison tool (latest revision)

key_numbers.note: Individualism=46 places Japan mid-range, not strongly collectivist. Hofstede's own data thus modestly supports Takano's critique.

papers.citation: Yamawaki, N. (2012). Within-culture variations of collectivism in Japan. Journal of Cross-Cultural Psychology, 43(8), 1191-1204.
papers.key_numbers: abstract only - validated Japanese Collectivism Scale (JCS), showed prefecture-level variation. Specific M/SD not retrieved.

papers.citation: Yanagida et al. (2024). Development and validation of the Japanese version of the Auckland Individualism and Collectivism Scale. Frontiers in Psychology, 15:1448461.
papers.file: not_accessible (open access but PDF fetch returned binary, abstract via WebFetch)

key_numbers.subscale_means_SD: not_accessible (not reported in main text per WebFetch summary)

self_esteem.summary: Strong, consistent evidence that Japanese score LOWER on RSES than international samples. Schmitt & Allik 2005 (53 nations) ranks Japan lowest. Oshio meta-analyses provide robust Japanese age/gender norms.

papers.citation: Schmitt, D. P., & Allik, J. (2005). Simultaneous administration of the Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale in 53 nations. JPSP, 89(4), 623-642.

key_numbers.japan_rank: lowest of 53 nations on overall RSES
key_numbers.japan_mean: not_accessible_exact (need full paper; secondary sources confirm Japan = lowest but no exact M)
key_numbers.note: Schmitt & Allik also flag a neutral response bias more prevalent in collectivist cultures, partially explaining low Japan scores.

papers.citation: Mimura, C., & Griffiths, P. (2007). A Japanese version of the Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale: Translation and equivalence assessment. Journal of Psychosomatic Research, 62(5), 589-594.

key_numbers.factor_structure: nearly identical between English and Japanese versions; target rotation confirmed factorial agreement
key_numbers.cronbach_alpha: reported as high for both versions (exact value not_accessible)

papers.citation: 小塩真司・岡田涼・茂垣まどか・並川努・脇田貴文 (2014). 自尊感情平均値に及ぼす年齢と調査年の影響―Rosenbergの自尊感情尺度日本語版のメタ分析―. 教育心理学研究, 62(4), 273-282.

age_effects_on_per_item_mean.junior_high_high_school: B = -0.23 (95%CI -0.29 to -0.17), β = -.40, lower than uni students
age_effects_on_per_item_mean.adult_18-60: B = +0.30 (95%CI 0.24 to 0.37), β = +.44, higher than uni students
age_effects_on_per_item_mean.elderly_60plus: B = +0.27 (95%CI 0.15 to 0.39), β = +.21, higher than uni students

key_numbers.year_effect: B = -0.01 per year (β = -.22, p<.001), self-esteem declining over time
key_numbers.response_format_effect: 5-point format yields ~0.10 higher per-item mean than 4-point

papers.citation: 小塩真司・脇田貴文・岡田涼・並川努・茂垣まどか (2014). 日本における自尊感情の時間横断的メタ分析: 得られた知見とそこから示唆されること. 発達心理学研究, 27(4), 299-311.

key_numbers.developmental_pattern: Decline through 10s, rise during university years, continued rise in middle/older adulthood; gender gap narrows from adolescence into adulthood
key_numbers.note: Aligns with Robins et al. 2002 and Orth et al. 2010 international longitudinal findings

authority.summary: Hofstede places Japan PDI=54 (mid-range, not high). Empirical RWA norm now exists for Japan (Takano et al. 2021).

papers.citation: 高野了太・高史明・野村理朗 (2021). 日本語版右翼権威主義尺度の作成. 心理学研究, 91(6), 398-408.

key_numbers.association_with_political_party: LDP supporters score higher RWA than opposition; aligns with Cambridge Japanese Journal of Political Science finding that authoritarian values predict LDP voting 2003-2019

papers.citation: Hofstede Insights — Japan Power Distance Index = 54

key_numbers.interpretation: Mid-range. Despite stereotypes of strict hierarchy, Japan's PDI is intermediate. Western standard sees it as moderate; Asian standard (e.g., Malaysia 100) sees Japan as not particularly hierarchical.

honne_tatemae.summary: No widely-used standardized 'honne/tatemae' Likert scale exists. The Japanese psychology literature treats honne-tatemae as a cultural-conceptual construct rather than a measured personality trait. Adjacent measured constructs: 愛想 (aisou/amiability), social desirability bias, self-monitoring. Mostly discussed qualitatively.

papers.citation: Ito, R., Navarro, A., & Takai, J. (2023). The Relationship between Mental Processes and Japan's Unique Communication Style of Aisou. Intercultural Communication Studies, 32(2), 38-?.

key_numbers.scale: Aisounoyosa scale (愛想の良さ) — 22 items, 5-point Likert (Ito 2020)
key_numbers.key_correlate: Compassion is the strongest internal-process driver of amiability; passive shyness reduces it; narcissism partially positive (self-presentation strategy).
key_numbers.honne_tatemae_link: Authors frame aisou as the tatemae side of self-presentation — closest existing scale capturing the tatemae construct empirically.

papers.citation: Search for dedicated 'honne/tatemae' scale (二面性/建前 measurement)

alternatives_used_in_literature: Social desirability scales (Marlowe-Crowne) — Japanese 'honne/tatemae' linked to higher SD bias
高田 自己の二面性 (Takada 1989, JJEP 37(4), 302-311) — referenced but PDF text extraction failed, specific data not_accessible
key_numbers.recommendation: Use aisou subscales or self-monitoring as proxy; flag in checklist that honne-tatemae itself is conceptual, not directly measured.

data_quality_caveats: RSES means above are converted to per-item 5-point scale by Oshio; multiply by 10 for total-score approximations on the original 4-point RSES would not be valid — use per-item.
Schmitt & Allik 2005 exact Japan mean remains not_accessible (paywall); only ranking confirmed.
Takada 1999 means are visible only in Table 6 as embedded image; full text indicates Japanese students score 相互協調性 > 相互独立性 but exact M values not extractable from the J-Stage PDF.
Mimura & Griffiths 2007 raw means could not be retrieved from any open source.
No honne/tatemae personality scale exists; the construct is treated culturally not psychometrically. Aisou scale (Ito 2020) is the closest empirical proxy.
_overall_notes.two_sided_view_on_collectivism: Required by user spec: this file records BOTH the 'Japan=collectivistic' tradition (Hofstede IDV=46, Markus & Kitayama 1991 theory, Schmitt & Allik finding low self-esteem consistent with self-criticism in interdependent cultures) AND the strong refutation (Takano & Osaka 1999/2018, Takano & Sogon 2008 — only ~14% of 43 studies support the common view).
